edges.description: The substitutions reduce the steady-state amount of MRPP1 protein rather than preventing its synthesis.
Reduced MRPP1 lowers the throughput of the 5'-cleavage reaction that releases mt-tRNAs from the polycistronic precursor.
Inefficient release of mt-tRNAs and mt-mRNAs from the precursor limits mitochondrial translation.
Fewer mtDNA-encoded subunits are available for assembly, so the complexes that contain them fail to accumulate.

nodes.description: Rare missense substitutions at evolutionarily conserved residues of MRPP1. Neither reported allele is truncating. In silico prediction was uninformative — the p.Arg181Leu substitution scores as relatively benign across SIFT, PolyPhen-2 and aGVGD — so pathogenicity rests on the functional work rather than on prediction, and the residue's proximity to the TRM10-type methyltransferase domain is a structural rather than a computed argument.

nodes.description: Reduced amounts of assembled complex I and complex IV, with complex III variably involved and complex II preserved. The defect is demonstrable both as reduced enzyme activity in skeletal muscle and as reduced assembled holocomplex on blue native PAGE, and in muscle it is patchy rather than uniform — COX deficiency is mosaic across fibres, with subsarcolemmal mitochondrial accumulation producing ragged red fibres.

nodes.description: Reduced de novo synthesis of the 13 mtDNA-encoded polypeptides. Because those 13 subunits are distributed across complexes I, III, IV and V but none sits in complex II, a translation-level lesion produces a characteristic biochemical signature: combined deficiency with complex II spared. This is the step that converts a single RNA-processing defect into a multi-complex respiratory chain phenotype.

nodes.description: Unprocessed precursor accumulates at the gene boundaries where cleavage should occur — RNA19 rises on northern blot, and RNA-seq shows increased read depth specifically across junctions requiring processing. The defect is one of efficiency, not of completion: mature mt-tRNA and mt-mRNA steady-state levels are largely normal, consistent with slower cleavage of a product that is itself stable once made. Because the 3' nuclease ELAC2 is intact in these patients, the predicted intermediate is an mt-mRNA still carrying an uncleaved tRNA at its 5' side.

nodes.description: MRPP1 steady-state levels fall in patient fibroblasts while its two RNase P partners, MRPP2 and MRPP3, are unchanged. The subunit stoichiometry of the holoenzyme is therefore skewed rather than the complex being globally lost, which is the opposite of the arrangement seen in MRPP2/HSD17B10 disease, where loss of MRPP2 secondarily drags MRPP1 down with it. Residual MRPP1 protein is present in both subjects, and the amount does not order the severity: the compound heterozygote had the lower MRPP1 level but the milder translation defect, implying the p.Arg181Leu protein is more stable but less active than p.Thr272Ala.
